title: LAD: Efficient Accelerator for Generative Inference of LLM with Locality Aware Decoding
problem: In LLM autoregressive decoding, the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length, and at lengths beyond 2048 tokens the attention mechanism's repeated read of the full KV cache becomes the dominant bottleneck, consuming over 50% of total inference time on GPU-based systems.
method: LAD (Locality Aware Decoding) is a dedicated ASIC accelerator that exploits numerical locality in attention scores across consecutive decoding steps. The key insight is that when an attention score at a specific sequence position remains approximately constant across several consecutive decoding steps, the corresponding key and value vectors need not be re-fetched at every step. LAD implements a locality detection engine that identifies stable-score positions and caches their contribution, dramatically reducing KV cache access frequency while maintaining decoding accuracy. The hardware includes specialized attention decoding units paired with on-chip score history buffers to track and exploit inter-step score locality.

title: A 100Gbaud 4Vppd Distributed Linear Driver with Cross-Folded Transmission Lines and Cross-Coupled Gm Cells for Built-in 5-Tap FFE in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS
problem: Linear pluggable optics (LPO) drivers must provide large output swing (high extinction ratio), high gain, and wide bandwidth simultaneously for short-reach fiber optics; conventional distributed amplifiers lack equalization, while transmission-line (TL) based FFE designs cannot achieve both high gain and large swing.
method: A distributed linear driver using cross-folded transmission lines and cross-coupled Gm cells that achieves both high gain and large output swing (4 Vppd). The transmission lines provide dual functionality: (1) passive frequency-response shaping for bandwidth extension, and (2) passive delay-line FFE implementation with 5 programmable taps for equalization.

title: 30.3 A 24Gb 42.5Gb/s GDDR7 DRAM with Low-Power WCK Distribution, an RC-Optimized Dual-Emphasis TX, and Voltage/Time-Margin-Enhanced Power Reduction
problem: GDDR7 DRAM must achieve 42.5Gb/s data rates while managing power consumption and thermal throttling in high-performance AI systems requiring extensive datasets and GPU processing.
method: The design introduces low-power write-clock (WCK) distribution, an RC-optimized dual-emphasis transmitter (TX), and voltage/time-margin-enhanced techniques to reduce power while maintaining high bandwidth PAM3 signaling at 42.5Gb/s.

title: Boosting Scientific Error-Bounded Lossy Compression through Optimized Synergistic Lossy-Lossless Orchestration
problem: Scientific workflows on GPUs produce high-throughput data requiring fast error-bounded compression; existing solutions sacrifice ratio or throughput.
method: cuSZ-Hi: GPU-optimized error-bounded lossy compressor combining optimized interpolation-based prediction and lossless encoding pipelines.

title: Streaming X-ray Detector Data to Remote Facilities Using EJFAT
problem: Real-time transfer and analysis of high-throughput scientific data to remote facilities

title: High-Performance Branch-Free Algorithms for Extended-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic
problem: Existing algorithms for extended-precision floating-point arithmetic (double, triple, quadruple precision) either use complex branching logic or are only correct on specific input classes, limiting performance and generality.
method: New branch-free algorithms for double, triple, and quadruple precision floating-point arithmetic with computer-verified correctness proofs for all IEEE floating-point inputs (within overflow/underflow thresholds).

title: 14.1 A 22nm 104.5TOPS/W µ-NMC-Δ-IMC Heterogeneous STT-MRAM CIM Macro for Noise-Tolerant Bayesian Neural Networks
problem: Image recognition under noise (environmental interference) degrades accuracy in CNNs and ViTs. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) offer better noise tolerance but implementing them in edge hardware requires efficient in-memory computing while handling μ-weight (mean) and Δ-weight (deviation) representations.
method: Heterogeneous STT-MRAM CIM macro combining μ-NMC (mean computation) and Δ-IMC (deviation in-memory compute) paths, processing mean and delta weight components separately with optimized circuitry for each. Leverages STT-MRAM for efficient weight storage.

title: Instruction-Aware Cooperative TLB and Cache Replacement Policies
problem: Modern server and data center applications have large instruction footprints that cause frequent instruction-side TLB and cache misses, with instruction TLB (iTLB) misses being particularly harmful because they cause pipeline stalls that block forward progress. Existing TLB and cache replacement policies treat instruction and data streams equivalently and do not account for the criticality of instruction accesses.
method: The paper proposes instruction-aware cooperative replacement policies that distinguish instruction accesses from data accesses in both the TLB and cache. The cooperative approach coordinates eviction decisions between the iTLB and the instruction cache (iCache), so that evicting a page from the iTLB also triggers or informs iCache eviction decisions and vice versa, reducing redundant refills. Replacement decisions are guided by instruction-access frequency and recency, with policy cooperation preventing the two structures from working at cross-purposes during instruction working set thrashing.

title: Cascade: A Dependency-aware Efficient Training Framework for Temporal Graph Neural Network
problem: TGNN training is severely constrained by temporal dependencies between input events: large batches improve parallelism but cause infrequent node memory updates leading to stale information and accuracy degradation, forcing small-batch training with high latency and underutilized hardware.
method: Cascade uses a topology-aware scheduler that packs as many spatially-independent events as possible into the same batch, then leverages inter-node memory similarity to identify 'stabilized' nodes whose memories have converged sufficiently to safely break temporal dependencies. This similarity-based dependency breaking allows temporally-independent events to be included in larger batches. An adaptive update frequency mechanism based on runtime feedback further reduces redundant memory updates, achieving 2.3x average (up to 5.1x) speedup without accuracy loss.

title: Memory: Almost The Only Thing That Matters : A revolution in memory architecture for the data center
problem: Data center performance bottleneck has shifted from computation to memory bandwidth and latency; traditional DRAM hierarchies and interconnects cannot keep pace with compute acceleration.
method: The work proposes architectural innovations in memory hierarchy, bandwidth, and interconnect design. Likely includes advanced memory technologies (HBM, 3D stacking), new interconnect protocols, and memory-compute co-design.

title: Testing and Benchmarking Emerging Supercomputers via the MFC Flow Solver
problem: New supercomputers require systematic testing and evaluation; lack of portable, user-friendly benchmarking tools limits adoption validation.
method: Multicomponent Flow Code (MFC) with automated toolchain for compilation, regression testing, and benchmarking across diverse hardware.

title: AutoPower: Automated Few-Shot Architecture-Level Power Modeling by Power Group Decoupling
problem: Traditional analytical architecture-level power models are inaccurate; recent ML-based approaches require sufficient training data from known configurations, which is unrealistic for early-stage power estimation with limited design configurations.
method: AutoPower decouples power consumption into independent power groups (e.g., clock, SRAM, logic) and builds individual ML models for each group based on correlations with structural information available at the architecture level. Further decoupling within power groups creates multiple sub-models, enabling accurate few-shot learning with minimal training data.

title: Augmenting Simulated Noisy Quantum Data Collection by Orders of Magnitude Using Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
problem: Classical simulation of noisy quantum systems requires 2^n x 2^n-dimensional density matrices for n qubits, making even moderate system sizes computationally intractable. Quantum trajectory methods reduce overhead but use unoptimized sampling, redundant state preparation, and single-shot data collection.
method: Pre-Trajectory Sampling technique optimizes trajectory simulation by: (1) tailoring error types to match experimental conditions, (2) batching sampling without redundant computation, (3) collecting error information efficiently. Evaluation on statevector simulation of 35-qubit quantum error-correction code and tensor network simulation of 85 qubits.

title: Dilu: Enabling GPU Resourcing-on-Demand for Serverless DL Serving via Introspective Elasticity
problem: Serverless DL serving systems use coarse-grained static GPU allocation that produces 15-94% GPU fragmentation due to dynamic workload patterns; existing horizontal-only scaling cannot adapt GPU resource allocation fine-grainedly within a running DL function instance, degrading utilization and violating QoS.
method: Dilu introduces Introspective Elasticity (IE), a two-dimensional co-scaling mechanism combining vertical scaling (adjusting GPU resource allocation within a running DL task) and horizontal scaling (adding/removing instances). Dilu uses multi-factor profiling with efficient pruning search to characterize each DL function's GPU compute/memory sensitivity. A cross-layer scheduler applies resourcing-complementary principles to fill fragmented GPU capacity with compatible DL tasks. At runtime, an adaptive 2D co-scaling controller continuously monitors QoS signals and adjusts both per-instance GPU allocation and the number of instances to minimize fragmentation while meeting SLAs.

title: A Blocker-Tolerant mm-Wave Low-Noise Amplifier Utilizing Doherty Active Load Modulation for Linearity Enhancement
problem: Emerging mm-wave applications (massive MIMO, automotive radar, SATCOM-on-the-Move, AR/VR) require high-linearity receivers/LNAs to handle multiple concurrent signals or weak signals amid strong interferers. Conventional LNA designs optimize for noise at weak signals but cannot maintain linearity with strong blockers.
method: Blocker-tolerant mm-wave LNA leveraging Doherty active load modulation to enhance linearity across wide input power range. Doherty architecture dynamically adjusts gain vs. linearity trade-off, maintaining output power efficiency under strong blockers.

title: Efficient Memory Side-Channel Protection for Embedding Generation in Machine Learning
problem: Embedding table lookups in ML models (DLRMs, LLMs) leak sensitive input features (user IDs, token indices) through memory access patterns, making them vulnerable to side-channel attacks; protecting these accesses with conventional ORAM incurs prohibitive overhead due to the massive size of embedding tables.
method: The paper evaluates three protection strategies: (1) linear scan of the embedding table (accesses all rows, hiding which row is used); (2) ORAM protection with optimized implementation; and (3) Deep Hash Embedding (DHE), which replaces the table lookup entirely with a hash-based neural network computation that takes the embedding index as input and produces an embedding vector through compute rather than memory access, eliminating the memory access pattern. A hybrid scheme combines DHE for large embedding tables (where its compute cost is amortized) with linear scan for small tables, selected per table based on profiled break-even points.
